# @uhop/vault-storage-mcp — full reference

Thin MCP (Model Context Protocol) adapter for vault-storage, an AI-agent-first
personal knowledge base: markdown files are the source of truth, a SQLite +
sqlite-vec index provides fast lookup, semantic search, and typed-edge
traversal. The adapter exposes the server's REST API as 63 MCP tools and 3
read-only resources. It is deliberately stateless — every call forwards to a
running vault-storage server; guards and validation live server-side so every
client gets them.

Plain JavaScript (ES modules), Node ≥ 26, stdio transport only (hono/express
never load at runtime).

## Install and configuration

Claude Code MCP config (`~/.claude/.mcp.json` or per-project `.claude/.mcp.json`):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "@uhop/vault-storage-mcp@latest"],
          "env": {
            "VAULT_API_URL": "http://your-host:8123",
            "VAULT_API_TOKEN": "<bearer-token>"
          }
        }
      }
    }

The bearer token is the `VAULT_API_TOKEN` the vault-storage server was started
with.

## Response-shape contract

Every tool description names the response shape it returns, including
conditional keys (absent unless their case is hit — their absence is not
evidence of anything) and which of the three list shapes it uses:

- paginated envelope `{items, offset, limit, total}` — page by `items.length`,
  never by the limit you asked for; the server caps `limit` at 100 and echoes
  what it used;
- flat `{count, items}` queue slices — unpaginated; a short result means raise
  the limit, not fetch a second page;
- genuinely unpaginated reads — everything arrives at once.

Input schemas inline closed-enum lists (record types, statuses, edge types,
suggestion kinds) so the canonical vocabulary is visible at discovery time.

## Tools (63)

Search & list:

- vault_search — lexical (FTS5, default) or semantic (mode=semantic) search;
  [{filename, score, matches}].
- vault_context_pack — one prepared RAG pack anchored by exactly one of
  `query` (hybrid: lexical FTS + semantic chunk-KNN, fused by reciprocal
  rank) or `record_id` (nearest chunks). Returns {anchor, chunks, graph,
  budget}; chunk text is the bare body segment the stored vectors index
  (degenerate segments skipped); the graph block carries the deduped 1-hop
  typed neighborhood as agent.summary lines — each entry with its typed
  edges + directions, inbound entries doubling as the backlinks
  (inbound_total = backlink degree), capped at 20 with the true total.
  The whole response is byte-budgeted chunks-first (default 32 KiB): the
  neighborhood trims before any chunk drops, then lowest-ranked chunks go,
  reported in budget.chunks_dropped and the neighborhood_total-vs-length
  gap — never silent. Replaces the search → similar → neighborhood → read
  chains.
- vault_list_pieces — filtered record listing (type, status, alias-aware tag,
  path prefix, updated_since…); paginated envelope.
- vault_list_folder — folder listing; unpaginated.

Read:

- vault_read_file — markdown by vault path; composes atomized folders;
  include_etag returns {path, etag, composed, content} for conditional writes.
- vault_read_piece — one record by id.
- vault_read_meta — the indexed record row minus body (not arbitrary FM keys).

Narrow writes (atomic server-side ops; prefer these over whole-document writes):

- vault_append — append to a body.
- vault_replace — asserted string replace (absent target 409s, ambiguous
  without all=true 409s with the count — never a silent no-op).
- vault_patch_fm — add/remove one frontmatter array member (related:, tags:…);
  echoes the resulting array.

Whole-document writes:

- vault_write_file / vault_update_piece — create or replace; optional
  expected_etag sent as If-Match (412 with details.current_etag on conflict);
  agent.derived_from_hash: "auto" is finalized server-side. Empty and
  literal-"null" bodies are refused by the server.
- vault_delete_file — removal (a note replaced by other content should be
  superseded instead).

Lifecycle:

- vault_supersede — replace a note, archiving the predecessor with its
  record_id (edges, embeddings, suggestions survive); successor gets a typed
  supersedes footer.
- vault_move — rename preserving record_id.
- vault_propose — search-before-write: score a draft against existing notes.

Maintenance:

- vault_raw_inbox — raw/ ready vs drafts split (the /vault ingest entry).
- vault_cleanup_lint — delete orphan embeddings and other auto-fixables.
- vault_embed_pending — embed records with missing/drifted vectors.
- vault_incremental_reindex — catch up after a git pull from another machine.
- vault_run_scans — all four suggestion-filing scans in one pass.

Tags:

- vault_list_tags — taxonomy listing; paginated envelope.
- vault_tag_info — one taxonomy row (requested appears on alias lookups).
- vault_records_by_tag — records carrying a tag (alias-aware; alias_for +
  requested on alias hits); paginated envelope.

Graph insight:

- vault_neighborhood — BFS layers + typed edges around a record (depth ≤ 5).
- vault_similar — embedding nearest neighbours; distance and score run in
  opposite directions (score = 1 - distance/2).
- vault_backlinks — inbound typed edges; paginated envelope.

Review queue:

- vault_list_suggestions (expand: "context" inlines per-item record briefs),
  vault_read_suggestion, vault_suggestions_summary — pending counts by kind.
- vault_claim_suggestions — reserve a batch under a holder with a TTL;
  vault_reopen_suggestion doubles as the explicit claim release.
- vault_accept_suggestion / vault_reject_suggestion — single decisions.
- vault_resolve_suggestions_batch — ≤ 100 decisions; mechanical tag/edge side
  effects applied server-side; per-item failures in results[].error.
- vault_create_suggestion — file a new suggestion.

Queue-item slices (flat {count, items}):

- vault_queue_top, vault_queue_ready, vault_queue_blocked,
  vault_queue_by_section, vault_queue_by_priority, vault_queue_by_project,
  vault_queue_project_archive; vault_queue_reindex rebuilds the derivative
  table after a multi-machine pull.

Repo leases (agent coordination — who may edit which repo working tree; flat
{count, items}, ephemeral: cleared on server restart):

- vault_lease_list — current leases; ?resource filters to one, same shape.
- vault_lease_claim — atomic claim/renew/preempt; 409 claimed_by_other with
  the current lease. Precedence: human > cwd agent > side agent; side claims
  attest a clean checkout ("clean at <sha>").
- vault_lease_renew, vault_lease_release (force = operator hatch),
  vault_lease_transfer — atomic handover, to_kind "human" for review/commit.
- vault_lease_events — append-only transcript, newest first.

Handoffs (agent coordination — role-addressed cross-agent work requests;
flat {count, items}; durable in the server-side spool, rebuilt by scan on
restart; resolved ones archive into projects/<project>/handoff-archive.md):

- vault_handoff_create — idempotency_key mandatory; a retry returns the
  original ({status: "existing"}). Addressed to a role (to:
  "repo:<normalized-remote-url>"), never a session; from is provenance only.
- vault_handoff_list — filters to/project/status/kind; the lease holder's
  inbox is status=open, a submitter's rework watch is status=returned.
- vault_handoff_get — the poller's read; watch status flip to
  done | rejected | returned.
- vault_handoff_claim — open → claimed; lazy claim expiry (default 30 min).
- vault_handoff_resolve — done | rejected (archives + clears the spool,
  returns archived_to) | returned (mandatory critique note; reopens the same
  record).
- vault_handoff_resubmit — returned → open after rework, same id.
- vault_handoff_note — append-only discussion; refused once resolved.
- vault_handoff_events — transcript, newest first (cleared on restart).
- vault_handoff_put_artifact — attach the transported work (agents cannot
  `git push`, so the spool is the transfer): `git format-patch --base=…`
  output as ext "patch", or a base64 "bundle" for binary/multi-branch. 10 MB
  cap (413 artifact_too_large). Replaces any existing artifact and sets the
  handoff's ref to {type: "spool"} — that ref type is server-set, never
  declared on create.
- vault_handoff_get_artifact — metadata {ext, bytes, sha256} by default;
  include_content: true to inline it. For anything large, stream it to a file
  with vault-curl instead, then `git apply --check` before `git am --3way`.

System:

- vault_status — indexer/DB state, embedder and memory blocks.
- vault_lint — integrity checks (nine categories) plus coverage.enrichment
  with the unenriched_records worklist; coverage never flips ok.
- vault_resume_bundle — one-shot session-start bundle (reindex + lint digest +
  suggestions + workflow + log summaries + project notes). The feedback body
  ships by default only while the whole bundle fits the server's 32 KiB
  budget; above it feedback arrives as summary + body_bytes + a headings
  index with body_omitted: {reason: "bundle_budget", budget_bytes}; naming
  files in project_bodies bypasses the budget.

## Resources

- vault://status — indexer state, schema version, counts
- vault://suggestions/pending — bulk pending review items
- vault://taxonomy/tags — managed tag taxonomy with counts

## Errors

Server errors surface as MCP tool errors (isError: true) with a JSON payload
{error, code, status, details}. Common codes: auth_failed, not_found,
conflict, replace_assert_failed (details.occurrences), precondition_failed
(details.current_etag), empty_body / null_body, network, bad_request,
validation_failed, internal.
